texto: Machine learning uses data to train a model.
Learning algorithms include machine learning and deep learning.
Database systems store and retrieve persistent records.
Supervised learning trains a model on labelled examples to predict new labels.
Unsupervised learning finds clusters in data without labels; K-Means is a classic example.
Deep learning stacks many neural network layers to learn representations from raw data.
A vector database stores embeddings produced by machine learning models.
Approximate nearest neighbor search trades a little recall for much faster queries.
Retrieval augmented generation looks up relevant documents before a language model answers.
Feature engineering turns raw data into inputs that a learning algorithm can use.
Overfitting happens when a model learns the training data too closely and generalizes poorly.
Cross validation estimates how well a machine learning model performs on unseen data.
Query optimization chooses an efficient execution plan for a database query.
An inverted index maps each term to the list of documents that contain it.
BM25 is a ranking function used by search engines to score documents for a query.
Gradient descent updates model parameters in the direction that reduces the loss.
Reinforcement learning trains an agent through rewards from its environment.
Transfer learning reuses a model trained on one task as the starting point for another.
Indexing structures such as B+ trees and hash tables speed up database lookups.
Distributed databases replicate and partition data across several machines.
